title: Quick Connect
description: Initiate, Connect, Authorize, AuthenticateWithQuickConnect; pending codes in Postgres with a short expiry so any api replica answers.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first: a rerunnable capture of Jellyfin 12.4 (compat/captures/quick-connect-12.4) records the status, body and fields of all five routes in each state: Quick Connect on by default and turned off; a code pending, approved, redeemed and expired; an unknown code and an unknown secret; Initiate missing each device field and carrying a stale token; approval naming yourself, naming another user as a viewer and as an administrator, and approving an already-approved code; redemption before approval, twice, and after the approving account is deleted; a device already signed in to the same account and to another one. It also records what jellyfin-web sends and shows on its login page and Quick Connect page, for a viewer and an administrator.
Each route answers what that capture records; every difference is listed in compat/differences.yaml with its reason, and a check asks jellyscale the capture's requests.

Moonfin (Moonfin-Core at a pinned commit, D-030) signs in with a code approved in jellyfin-web, then plays a film; the run records the device or emulator. An app whose player sends no token is not a target (D-026).
In jellyfin-web, a browser holding no token picks Use Quick Connect; a second browser signed in as a viewer approves the code; the first is then signed in as that viewer and plays a film.

Initiate, approval, every Connect poll and redemption can each be answered by a different api replica, run as separate processes; an api replica killed between any two steps loses no code, approval or token.

A code is six decimal digits, as Jellyfin's are. No code is live for two devices at once. Only the secret reads a code's state or redeems it; the code alone never yields a token. Connect's answer never carries a token.

A code not approved within 10 minutes of Initiate is gone: approval answers as for an unknown code, and Connect and redemption answer as for an unknown secret. An approved code can be redeemed only within the window the capture confirms after approval, never later.

Redeeming before approval answers 'not yet', as Jellyfin does, and the code can still be approved. When approval and redemption arrive at once on two replicas, the device gets either 'not yet' or its token, never an error.

If two accounts approve one code at once on two replicas, the device is signed in to exactly one of them; the other approval is refused and changes nothing. A later second approval is refused the same way.
Redeeming one secret twice, one after the other or at once on two replicas, never leaves the device with two live tokens.

Approval is always for the approver's own account, administrators included. A userId naming the caller, missing, or empty (as jellyfin-web's administrator page may send it) approves for the caller. Naming anyone else answers 403 and leaves the code pending. This differs from Jellyfin and is listed in compat/differences.yaml.

The token belongs to the device that asked for the code: its DeviceId, name, app and version, as /Sessions shows. It works on api and stream replicas like a token from a password sign-in. The approver's own token keeps working.

If the asking device already holds a token for the approver's account, that old token is replaced and answers 401. A token the device holds for another account is kept. Both match what a password sign-in on that device does.

Initiate without DeviceId, Device, Client or Version is refused as Jellyfin refuses it, and nothing is stored. Initiate, Connect and redemption read no token, so a stale, revoked or unknown token sent with them changes nothing.
An account deleted after approving redeems nothing: the device gets the unknown-secret answer and no token. The same holds for a disabled account if JS-033 has landed first.

The guessing bound (D-078): failed approvals (an unknown, expired or already-approved code) are counted per approving account only. After 10 failures within 15 minutes, approvals by that account are refused for 15 minutes with 403 and Retry-After, and the refusal checks no code, counts toward nothing and does not lengthen itself. The account's tokens, playback and password sign-in go on. The bound holds across two replicas and restarts; 200 approvals sent at once check no more than 10 codes. Connect polling and redemption are never refused.

Nothing is refused for polling. Ten devices behind one address, each polling Connect every 5 seconds well past their code's expiry, are all answered. Initiate, Connect and redemption count toward no bound.

The password bounds neither count nor refuse any Quick Connect route. A device approved by code signs in while the account's name is refused to strangers and while its address is refused for passwords (D-020). Afterwards it is a known device of the account for JS-145's per-device bound.

At most 100 live codes exist across all replicas, pending or approved and unredeemed; the cap is not configurable. Past it Initiate is refused, the status chosen from what jellyfin-web is observed to show, and no code already issued is touched, so a TV's code works for its full time. Each refusal is logged with its reason and counted in a metric. docs/access.md and docs/running.md state the cap and that password sign-in is unaffected.

Quick Connect is on by default, as in Jellyfin 12.4, and is turned off in configuration. When off: /QuickConnect/Enabled answers false and jellyfin-web shows no Quick Connect button; the other four routes answer 401, as in Jellyfin; Moonfin falls back to the password form only on Initiate's 401 (#104); a replica with it off gives no token for a code started before it was turned off.
Each refusal is logged with its bound or cap, the approving account (for D-078) and never a secret. Refusals are counted in a metric labelled by bound or cap only.
Initiate, Connect and AuthenticateWithQuickConnect are open to anyone, each with its reason. Authorize requires a viewer. TestAccess asks all five.

docs/access.md states how long a code lives, the 100-live-code cap, D-078's bound, the worst-case 960 guesses per account per day, and that Quick Connect is how a viewer gets in while their name is refused. docs/status.md and docs/running.md (the configuration key and its default, and the cap) are updated. These are deliverables, not things to test.
An approval in flight ends at shutdownGrace: forced with Postgres stalled and the client gone, the replica exits within seconds of the grace (D-097).
An approval that fails after its client hung up is logged at warn with the user and the reason, never the code (D-097).
notes: Requested by Fluster, the client that ships with jellyscale: #104. Access: approval is own, an administrator included. (access model, 2026-11-16) Needs its own guessing bound, following JS-145's design (product owner, 2026-11-19). Findroid is dropped as a target: the second client is one that sends its token on media requests (owner, 2026-11-20, D-026). D-078: failed approvals are bounded per approving account, 10 failures in 15 minutes then 15 minutes refused. D-079: at most 100 live codes; past the cap Initiate is refused, never an eviction. C (per-address Initiate caps) is backlog, promoted when the metric shows the cap reached. D-082: the TV journey for password and provider accounts alike.
